technologistSummary: Sleep efficiency was 85.2% with 358.0 minutes of total sleep time.
The synthetic respiratory summary contains 108 apneas/hypopneas for an AHI of 18.1 events/hour and 21 additional RERAs for an RDI of 21.6 events/hour.
Respiratory disturbance is more prominent in the supine position and during REM in this fictional example.
Oxygen saturation averaged 94%, with a synthetic nadir of 82% and 6.2 minutes below 88%.

All measurements and event counts on this page are fabricated for report-reading practice.

physician.name: Avery Morgan, MD
interpretation: This fictional diagnostic polysomnogram demonstrates an obstructive sleep-disordered breathing pattern. The overall respiratory disturbance is characterized in this teaching example as moderate obstructive sleep apnea, with greater event frequency while supine and during REM sleep.
Respiratory events are accompanied by oxygen desaturation, including a synthetic nadir of 82%. Central apneas are infrequent and do not dominate the respiratory disturbance in this example.
Periodic limb movements are present at a relatively low frequency and are associated with few arousals in this fictional study. No sustained cardiac arrhythmia is described in the synthetic report.
impressions: Fictional example: Moderate obstructive sleep apnea pattern, worse supine and in REM sleep.
Fictional example: Sleep-related oxygen desaturation associated with respiratory events.
Fictional example: Periodic limb movements present without a prominent PLM-related arousal burden in this report.
recommendations: Educational example: correlate the PSG findings with symptoms, medical history, physical examination, and treatment goals during a clinical sleep-medicine visit.

Educational example: discuss appropriate obstructive sleep apnea treatment options with the treating sleep clinician; the choice may depend on severity, anatomy, preferences, comorbidities, and other clinical factors.
Educational example: because the synthetic events are more frequent supine, positional information would be considered alongside the complete clinical picture rather than used in isolation.
Educational example: if therapy is started, follow-up should assess symptom response, treatment effectiveness, adherence when relevant, and any residual oxygenation or respiratory concerns.
